engines.name: MIGRATE Ω
engines.label: Autonomous Software Modernization
engines.source_mechanism: Reported Fable 5.2 long-horizon coding, multi-agent development and a production Python-to-Rust migration. Does not establish arbitrary migrations.
engines.product: Versioned, independently accepted migration packages with rollbacks; recurring compatibility and patch subscriptions.
engines.why_now: More long-horizon technical work becomes a candidate for bounded autonomous completion and lower complete cost.
engines.competitive_risk: Internal frontier agents and migration consultancies can already deliver many of the same outcomes.
engines.moat: Per-customer contract test corpus, dependency maps, deployment/rollback receipts and validated maintenance relationships.
engines.scalability: Reusable migration tools and domain adapters; internal human engineering per accepted customer must decline with volume.
engines.threshold: Prove full behavior preservation and lower complete costs than a competent human-plus-AI provider, including failures and support.
engines.first_sale: Buyer-approved small migration with a fixed acceptance suite and explicit rollback obligations.

engines.name: PROVE Ω
engines.label: Machine-Checked Software Assurance
engines.source_mechanism: DeepMind reported human-guided specification and AI-generated Lean proofs of selected compiled Signal security guarantees. Not a general available assurance agent.
engines.product: Verified theorem-and-executable bundles with independent proof replay and regression assurance.
engines.why_now: Proof automation may lower human proof-engineering cost for precisely specified software properties.
engines.competitive_risk: Expert formal-methods teams, existing provers, and conventional tests may be superior on many scopes.
engines.moat: Customer-approved specifications, trusted proof checkers and repeatable evidence on compiled releases.
engines.scalability: Reuse theorem templates and proof infrastructure; independent specification expertise remains a material bottleneck.
engines.threshold: Independent proof recheck on an authorized bounded target plus known-bug mutants, and fully loaded economics versus specialists.
engines.first_sale: Narrow signed verification scope of a selected library property and exact compiled artifact.

engines.name: TRUST Ω
engines.label: Verifiable Model Inference
engines.source_mechanism: FlashProve open source large-MoE zkSNARK prototype; 400B model 110 proved tokens/s on H100 under quantized greedy conditions, with reported 70-95x GPU overhead.
engines.product: Portable independent verification receipts for explicitly supported inference configurations and audited workloads.
engines.why_now: Open prototype dramatically lowers barriers to experimenting with large-model cryptographic receipts.
engines.competitive_risk: Provider signatures, TEEs, selective recomputation, audits and alternative proof providers are much cheaper for many buyers.
engines.moat: Verification integrations, managed statements, low-friction receipt checking and customer-specific assurance profiles.
engines.scalability: Reusable verifier SDK and asynchronous selective proving; proof costs are paid, not magically eliminated.
engines.threshold: Proof verifier accepts genuine receipt, rejects tampering, meets actual cost/latency/privacy constraints and beats buyers’ best alternatives.
engines.first_sale: Paid enterprise pilot of post-hoc proofs for a tightly scoped sensitive workload.

engines.name: LAB Ω
engines.label: Autonomous Design-to-Prototype
engines.source_mechanism: Anthropic reported three Fable 5.2-designed PCB/software/enclosure devices manufactured with partner Diode; independent transferability and unit economics unproved.
engines.product: Design-to-independent-bench-accepted electronics with versioned manufacturing files, firmware and reuse licenses.
engines.why_now: Agentic design/EDA integration can shorten qualified hardware design iteration for low-risk devices.
engines.competitive_risk: Experienced electronics contractors, CAD automation and electronics design platforms already operate efficiently.
engines.moat: Verified test fixtures, design rule libraries, component availability and manufacturer relationships.
engines.scalability: Contract manufacturing scales beyond a sole founder but retains real external human assembly and physical QA costs.
engines.threshold: Three held-out design/test scenarios on a fixed budget with qualified bench evidence and zero undisclosed safety assumptions.
engines.first_sale: Customer-funded low-risk measurement or interface board with pre-agreed bench tests.

engines.name: WORKCELL Ω
engines.label: Verified Cross-Application Outcomes
engines.source_mechanism: Terra release reports lower cost per computer-use task and higher benchmark accuracy; no individual production SOP is independently qualified.
engines.product: Outcome-priced reconciliations and cross-application workflows with independent state receipts and recovery.
engines.why_now: Improved visual understanding and cost can bring some previously uneconomic exception-heavy workflows within reach.
engines.competitive_risk: APIs, Zapier-style platforms, established RPA, internal IT and other computer-use agents can win on complete costs.
engines.moat: Customer-approved action policies, resilient connectors, state-checking oracles, exception-case memory.
engines.scalability: Self-service workflow configuration, reused connectors and subscription contracts with bounded exceptions.
engines.threshold: Unseen cross-app state acceptance, retries and idempotence outperform API/RPA with complete support and remediation costs.
engines.first_sale: A fully permissioned recurring two-system reconciliation with before/after state-based acceptance.
